headline: Ethereum Comptroller proxy and implementation both verified on Etherscan; public multi-repo GitHub org; multiple recognized-firm audits including a September 2025 Certik/Quantstamp audit directly covering the BNB Chain Core Pool Comptroller Diamond facets

findings.text: Ethereum Core Pool Comptroller (0x687a01ecF6d3907658f7A7c714749fAC32336D1B) is verified on Etherscan as a proxy contract (abiSource: 'etherscan', verified: true), with implementation resolved to 0xC910F2B196C516253e88b2097ba5D7d5fC9fa84e — both covered by the merged ABI. BNB Chain and Arbitrum on-chain verification could not be confirmed in this run due to API chain limitations (BSCScan) and access restrictions.

The official VenusProtocol GitHub organisation hosts multiple public repositories: venus-protocol (BNB Chain Core Pool Diamond Comptroller and VToken contracts), isolated-pools (Ethereum/Arbitrum/Base/Optimism/Unichain Comptroller contracts), governance-contracts, oracle, and protocol-reserve. The Ethereum Comptroller ABI shape (constructor with poolRegistry_, Comptroller name) corresponds to the isolated-pools Comptroller codebase per repo README. No specific commit SHA was pinned for deployed contracts in this run; this is recorded as a scope limit below.

The Venus security-and-audits documentation page (https://docs-v4.venus.io/links/security-and-audits) lists comprehensive audit coverage. Most recent Core Pool Comptroller-relevant audits: (1) E-Mode support — Certik audit 2025-09-19 and Quantstamp audit 2025-09-03, both scoped to Diamond Comptroller facets (MarketFacet.sol, PolicyFacet.sol, RewardFacet.sol, SetterFacet.sol, Diamond.sol) and VToken.sol on BNB Chain; (2) Risk Stewards V1 / Core Pool Comptroller Interface Compatibility — Certik 2025-02-19, Quantstamp 2025-02-13, FairyProof 2025-02-26; (3) Unlist markets — Certik 2024-04-09; (4) Diamond Comptroller — OpenZeppelin 2023-08-17, Certik, Peckshield, Quantstamp, Fairyproof (2023). For Isolated Pools Comptroller (Ethereum etc.): Code4rena 2023-05-15, Certik, Peckshield, Hacken (2023); Time-based contracts — Certik 2024-01-17, Quantstamp 2024-03-19. The pinned audit link (certik.org/projects/swipe) was access-blocked; all other audit PDFs are accessible via GitHub-hosted links.

Audit firms confirmed as broadly recognised: OpenZeppelin (Diamond Comptroller 2023, Venus Prime 2023, Token Converters 2023, Multichain Governance 2024), Certik (multiple reports 2023–2025), Peckshield (multiple reports 2023), Quantstamp (multiple reports 2023–2025), Hacken (Isolated Pools, Oracles 2023). All are on the recognised-firm list. Additionally Cantina (2024) and Pessimistic (2024, 2025) appear for peripheral contracts.

The most recent Core Pool Comptroller audit (E-Mode, Certik 2025-09-19 and Quantstamp 2025-09-03) directly covers the Diamond Comptroller facets deployed on BNB Chain. This is approximately 8 months prior to analysis date 2026-05-07. No diff between the audit commit and current deployed bytecode was performed in this run — recorded as a scope limit in unknowns[]. The audit scope per the docs covers the exact fund-custody Comptroller contracts.

Ethereum Comptroller proxy (0x687a01ecF6d3907658f7A7c714749fAC32336D1B) and implementation (0xC910F2B196C516253e88b2097ba5D7d5fC9fa84e) are both resolved and verified by Etherscan, confirmed via defipunkd /api/contract/abi which auto-resolves the proxy and returns abiSource: 'etherscan' with merged ABI. For BNB Chain (Diamond proxy, chainId 56), verification could not be confirmed via the defipunkd API (chain not supported); BSCScan not directly fetched.

steelman.red: The primary chain (BNB) bytecode verification was not confirmed in this run, the pinned audit link (certik.org/projects/swipe) returns an access error, and no commit-to-bytecode match was performed for any chain — leaving the verification claim resting on secondary evidence.
steelman.orange: The E-Mode audit from September 2025 is ~8 months old (borderline for the ≤6 months drift rule), and BNB Chain on-chain verification was not confirmed in this run; additionally, the contract system spans 8 chains with different codebases (Diamond Comptroller on BNB vs isolated-pools Comptroller elsewhere), and not all chain deployments have equal recent audit coverage.
steelman.green: Ethereum Comptroller proxy + implementation are both confirmed verified on Etherscan via the defipunkd read API; multiple public GitHub repos exist under the VenusProtocol org; and the E-Mode audit (Certik 2025-09-19, Quantstamp 2025-09-03) directly covers the BNB Chain Core Pool Comptroller Diamond facets — the most security-critical contracts — with recognised firms, less than 12 months before the analysis date, and an ongoing retainer-style audit programme with OpenZeppelin and others.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the Ethereum Comptroller proxy and implementation are both confirmed verified on Etherscan (evidence from defipunkd /api/contract/abi, fetched this run); two public GitHub repos (venus-protocol for BNB, isolated-pools for all other chains) exist whose contract structure matches the deployed ABIs; and the most recent Core Pool Comptroller audit (Certik 2025-09-19 + Quantstamp 2025-09-03) directly covers the BNB Chain Diamond Comptroller facets from a broadly recognised firm within 8 months of analysis date. The orange steel-man is weaker because: (a) the 6-month cutoff is a soft downgrade signal, not a hard rule per the rubric, and the audit programme is continuous; (b) BNB Chain verification is not refuted, merely unconfirmed in this run; (c) the Venus documentation lists all audit PDFs hosted in their own GitHub repos, providing strong traceability even without the blocked certik.org link.

evidence.shows: Ethereum Core Pool Comptroller (0x687a01ec...) is verified on Etherscan (verified: true, abiSource: 'etherscan'), is a proxy with implementation resolved to 0xC910F2B196C516253e88b2097ba5D7d5fC9fa84e; merged ABI returned

Ethereum Comptroller surfacer page confirms proxy → implementation 0xC910F2B196C516253e88b2097ba5D7d5fC9fa84e, ABI source etherscan, and live view-method results including owner() returning the Normal Timelock 0xd969E79...

Official VenusProtocol/venus-protocol repository is public; contains contracts/ (Comptroller Diamond facets, VToken, etc.), audits/ directory, and deployments/ directory; README confirms Diamond proxy Comptroller architecture on BNB Chain

Venus official security-and-audits page lists: E-Mode Core Pool Comptroller audit by Certik (2025-09-19) and Quantstamp (2025-09-03) covering Diamond Comptroller facets; Risk Stewards / Core Pool Comptroller Interface by Certik (2025-02-19), Quantstamp (2025-02-13), FairyProof (2025-02-26); Diamond Comptroller by OpenZeppelin (2023-08-17), Certik, Peckshield, Quantstamp, Fairyproof (2023); Isolated Pools by Certik, Peckshield, Hacken, Code4rena (2023); multichain governance by OpenZeppelin (2024-01-19), Certik, Cantina, Quantstamp (2024). All audit PDFs are hosted in VenusProtocol GitHub repos.

VenusProtocol/isolated-pools is the public repository containing the Comptroller and VToken contracts deployed on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Unichain etc. (the isolated-pool architecture used for Core Pool on non-BNB chains per repo README)

protocol_metadata.about: Venus Core Pool is a decentralized algorithmic money market protocol deployed across BNB Chain and seven other EVM networks, where users supply and borrow crypto assets (BNB, BEP-20, and ERC-20 tokens) to earn interest or take leverage. On BNB Chain the Comptroller is implemented as a Diamond proxy with multiple facets (MarketFacet, PolicyFacet, RewardFacet, SetterFacet); on other chains it uses the isolated-pools Comptroller architecture. The protocol uses a Resilient Price Oracle with multiple sources (Chainlink, RedStone, Binance Oracle) and is governed by XVS token-weighted voting via Governor Bravo with Normal, FastTrack, and Critical timelocks.
